title: What if everyone turned 6 for 5 seconds?

vo.text: What if everyone turned six... for five seconds?
The average American adult? Five foot six.
Second one. Everyone drops twenty inches,
and three quarters of their weight.
Shoes slip off. Grip strength? Down eighty percent.
Second two. Every seat belt now crosses a six year old's neck.
Adult belts fit at four foot nine and up.
Second three. Nobody can reach the brake.
At twenty five miles an hour, that's thirty seven feet... every second.
Second four. Most new cars... brake themselves.
The old taxi? Not so much.
Its airbag fires... at a six year old.
Their heads barely shrank. By six, the brain is about ninety percent adult size.
Who was in more danger: the kids walking... or the kids driving?
